citation: Fick, S.E. & Hijmans, R.J. (2017). WorldClim 2: new 1km spatial resolution climate surfaces for global land areas. International Journal of Climatology, 37(12), 4302–4315.
preprocessing_notes: Resample to 1 km COG, clip to AOI. BIO1=Annual Mean Temp; BIO12=Annual Precipitation; BIO15=Precipitation Seasonality most relevant for agroforestry suitability.
limitations: 30-year climatological mean; does not capture interannual variability or extremes. Resolution may mask local topographic effects. Not for: Site-level microclimate analysis or real-time weather monitoring
description: Global gridded bioclimatic variables (BIO1-BIO19) derived from 1970-2000 monthly temperature and precipitation.

citation: Karger, D.N. et al. (2017). Climatologies at high resolution for the earth's land surface areas (CHELSA). Scientific Data, 4, 170122.
preprocessing_notes: Resample to 1 km COG. CHELSA-BIOCLIM+ Version 1.2 used by Yadav et al. (2024) for agroforestry suitability in Punjab. Use Bio1 (Annual Mean Temp), Bio12 (Annual Precipitation), Tmax_Jan, Tmax_May.
limitations: Statistical downscaling from ERA5; may show artefacts in complex terrain. Less validated over Africa and Central Asia. Not for: Short-term weather forecasting or sub-field precision agriculture
description: Bias-corrected high-resolution global bioclimatic variables, climatology 1981-2010 (~1 km).

citation: Poggio, L. et al. (2021). SoilGrids 2.0: producing soil information for the globe with quantified spatial uncertainty. SOIL, 7, 217–240.
preprocessing_notes: Extract layers at 0–30 cm depth (topsoil) and 30–60 cm (subsoil). Resample to 1 km. pH, SOC, clay content, CEC are primary agroforestry suitability constraints per Ahmad et al. (2020), Chuma et al. (2021), Haile (2024).
limitations: Prediction uncertainty is high in data-sparse regions (much of sub-Saharan Africa). Point observations biased toward accessible areas. Temporal static — does not capture land-use change effects on soil. Not for: Precision soil management at plot level; nutrient management plans without ground-truthing
description: Global digital soil mapping (250 m) of physical and chemical soil properties at six depths.

citation: Farr, T.G. et al. (2007). The Shuttle Radar Topography Mission. Reviews of Geophysics, 45(2), RG2004.
preprocessing_notes: Derive slope (degrees) and aspect from DEM in GEE. Slope is primary biophysical constraint for agroforestry machinery access and erosion risk. Used across nearly all 23 AF papers in stocktake (Ahmad et al. 2017, 2018, 2020; Chuma et al. 2021; Haile 2024; Nath et al. 2021; Mushtaq et al. 2023; Seja et al. 2022; Wotlolan et al. 2021).
limitations: Voids in high-relief areas filled with ASTER or other interpolation methods — check for artefacts. Vegetation canopy not filtered — potential overestimation of elevation under forest cover. Not for: Hydraulic modelling requiring bare-earth DEM; landslide hazard at plot scale
description: Shuttle Radar Topography Mission digital elevation model, 3 arc-second (~90 m), 56°S-60°N.

citation: Zanaga, D. et al. (2022). ESA WorldCover 10m 2021 v200. Zenodo.
preprocessing_notes: Reclassify to agricultural mask (cropland, grassland, sparse vegetation) to define eligible agroforestry conversion area. Exclude built-up, water bodies, bare soil with high salinity. Aggregate to 100m or 1km for pipeline. Used as LULC base by multiple AF studies.
limitations: Mixed-pixel confusion in fragmented agricultural landscapes. Annual snapshot — does not capture seasonal cultivation. Accuracy lower in arid landscapes and under cloud cover. Not for: Crop-type mapping; sub-field land use classification
description: ESA WorldCover 10 m global land-cover map (2021), Sentinel-1/2 derived 11-class classification.

citation: UNEP-WCMC & IUCN (2024). Protected Planet: The World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA). Cambridge: UNEP-WCMC and IUCN.
preprocessing_notes: Rasterize to 100m. Hard exclusion mask for IUCN categories Ia, Ib, II for agroforestry suitability (conversion not permitted). Categories V, VI may allow agroforestry within management plans — flag as conditional. Used by Chuma et al. (2021) as exclusion layer around Itombwe Nature Reserve.
limitations: Boundary data quality varies by country. Some protected areas are paper parks with little enforcement. Does not capture community conserved areas (OECMs) comprehensively. Not for: Legal compliance decisions; site-level permitting
description: World Database on Protected Areas — global polygons of legally protected sites (UNEP-WCMC / IUCN).

dataset_name: FAO Global Soil Organic Carbon Map (GSOCmap) v1.6.1
citation: FAO & ITPS (2018). Global Soil Organic Carbon Map (GSOCmap) v1.6.1. Technical Report. FAO, Rome.
preprocessing_notes: Use as carbon co-benefit layer in opportunity space. Mendonça et al. (2023) use SOC sequestration potential as an agroforestry prioritisation criterion. Kiziridis et al. (2026) map silvopastoral carbon sequestration. Complement with FAO GSOCseq for sequestration rate.
limitations: Country submissions vary in quality and methodology. National and sub-national SOC maps (where available) should be used in preference. Not for: Carbon crediting baselines without country-specific validation; REDD+ baseline setting
description: FAO Global Soil Organic Carbon map — country-validated 1 km topsoil (0-30 cm) SOC stocks.

citation: Fick, S.E. & Hijmans, R.J. (2017). WorldClim 2: new 1km spatial resolution climate surfaces for global land areas. International Journal of Climatology, 37(12), 4302-4315.
preprocessing_notes: Rainfall is the second most frequent input variable (38 of 85 papers). Extract mean annual precipitation and wet-season monthly totals. Use for SCS-CN runoff depth calculation combined with HSG soil map. Buraihi & Shariff (2015) use projected precipitation to assess future RWH viability under climate change.
limitations: 30-year climatological mean; interannual variability not captured. Resolution too coarse for localised orographic precipitation in complex terrain. Not for: Flood frequency analysis; design-storm estimation for dam sizing
description: Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Stations, ~5 km daily precipitation 1981-present.

citation: Farr et al. (2007). SRTM. Reviews of Geophysics.
preprocessing_notes: WH module alias for SRTM. See srtm_dem_90m entry for full notes.
limitations: Voids in high-relief terrain. Not for: Engineering design
description: Shuttle Radar Topography Mission digital elevation model, 1 arc-second (~30 m), 56°S-60°N.

citation: Fick & Hijmans (2017). WorldClim 2. International Journal of Climatology.
preprocessing_notes: Extract mean annual precipitation and wet-season monthly totals for SCS-CN runoff calculation.
limitations: 30-year climatological mean; interannual variability not captured. Not for: Flood frequency analysis; design-storm estimation
description: WorldClim v2 monthly precipitation (1970-2000) at ~1 km.

citation: IFPRI MapSPAM 2020 v2r2; CGIAR Climate Action Data Hub, https://cgiar-climate-data-hub.github.io/catalog/spam2020/
preprocessing_notes: Select cocoa (coco) band 34 from physical_area/all COG; divide hectares by pixel hectares. Positive fraction is host presence; retain fraction for extent. Not a graded suitability score.
limitations: ~10 km; allocation-model estimate, not observed. Coarse for sub-national targeting. Not for: plot siting.
description: MapSPAM 2020 — gridded crop production allocation for cocoa at ~10 km.

dataset_name: Gridded Livestock of the World v4 (GLW4, 2020)
citation: FAO (2024). Gridded Livestock of the World 4, 2020. https://www.fao.org/livestock-systems/global-distributions/en/
preprocessing_notes: Hosted species COGs: https://digital-atlas.s3.amazonaws.com/cdh/data/glw4-2020/cog/glw4-2020-{species}.tif ; species cattle, buffalo, goat, sheep for ruminants. Units head/km2; preserve nodata. Do not treat modelled livestock presence as confirmed grazing management.
limitations: Census-downscaled modelled density at 5 arc-minutes; pastoral mobility and housed animals limit grazing inference.
description: FAO GLW4 modelled densities for buffalo, cattle, chicken, goat, pig and sheep; 2020 reference year.

citation: Didan, K. (2021). MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 250m SIN Grid V061. NASA EOSDIS Land Processes DAAC.
preprocessing_notes: Aggregate to annual mean / max-NDVI / range as needed. Mask cloud-flagged pixels per QA layer.
limitations: Coarser than Sentinel-2; for finer NDVI use Sentinel-2 SR. Cloud contamination in tropics.
description: NASA MODIS Terra Vegetation Indices MOD13Q1 — 16-day composite NDVI at 250m. The de facto standard NDVI surface for time-series + annual aggregation.

dataset_name: Global accessibility to cities — Weiss et al. (Nelson) 2018, 2015 baseline
citation: Weiss, D. J., et al. (2018). A global map of travel time to cities to assess inequalities in accessibility in 2015. Nature, 553, 333-336.
preprocessing_notes: Travel time minutes; invert if framing as accessibility (1 / time) for the suitability surface.
limitations: Road network from OSM ~2016; coverage variable in remote regions; not updated for post-2016 infrastructure.
description: Global travel time to the nearest city of 50,000+ inhabitants at ~1 km. Built from road network, terrain, surface friction and city polygons.

citation: Elvidge, C. D., et al. (2021). Annual time series of global VIIRS nighttime lights derived from monthly averages: 2012 to 2019. Remote Sensing, 13(5), 922.
preprocessing_notes: Use as continuous radiance or threshold (e.g. >1 nW/cm²/sr) for binary 'grid-served'.
limitations: Proxy only — captures lit pavement + industrial flaring, not domestic-only electrification.
description: NOAA Earth Observation Group VIIRS DNB annual cloud-free composite at ~500m — radiance values used as electrification proxy.

dataset_name: LandMark — Global Platform of Indigenous & Community Lands
citation: LandMark Consortium (2024). LandMark: Global Platform of Indigenous and Community Lands. World Resources Institute and partners.
preprocessing_notes: Spatial join with AOI; flag overlap as FPIC_REQUIRED for M6 hand-off.
limitations: Coverage is patchy — only countries where IPLC mapping is documented; absence ≠ no IPLC presence.
description: Global vector platform of indigenous and community lands — formal recognition status, customary tenure boundaries.

dataset_name: ACLED — Armed Conflict Location & Event Data
citation: Raleigh, C., Linke, A., Hegre, H., & Karlsen, J. (2010). Introducing ACLED-Armed Conflict Location and Event Data. Journal of Peace Research, 47(5), 651-660.
preprocessing_notes: Aggregate events per km² over a rolling window (e.g. 5 years); pair with WB FCV admin0 list.
limitations: Event detection bias (media-coverage-dependent); under-reporting in less-mediated conflicts.
description: Point-event conflict dataset (battles, violence, riots, protests) with daily updates. Used here as gridded event density for fragility framing.

citation: Kaufmann, D., Kraay, A., & Mastruzzi, M. (2010). The Worldwide Governance Indicators: Methodology and Analytical Issues. World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 5430.
preprocessing_notes: Use the 'government effectiveness' indicator as the default extension/governance proxy; composite across all six if a broader index is needed.
limitations: Country-level only; no subnational variation — qualified-flag-only for in-country MCDA differentiation (per T5 spatial-grain rule).
description: WB WGI — six aggregate governance indicators (voice/accountability, political stability, government effectiveness, regulatory quality, rule of law, control of corruption), admin0, annual.

citation: Demirgüç-Kunt, A., Klapper, L., Singer, D., & Ansar, S. (2022). The Global Findex Database 2021: Financial Inclusion, Digital Payments, and Resilience in the Age of COVID-19. World Bank.
preprocessing_notes: Use 'account ownership' or 'borrowed from formal financial institution' as the rural-finance proxy; subnational requires_upload via national surveys.
limitations: Survey-based, country-level only; subnational requires_upload.
description: WB Global Findex — financial inclusion indicators (account ownership, savings, credit, mobile money). Survey-based, admin0, triennial.

citation: FAO (2024). FAOSTAT statistical database. Rome: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations.
preprocessing_notes: Use producer prices + trade volumes as a market-depth proxy; subnational requires country-team uploads.
limitations: Admin0 granularity; subnational variation invisible.
description: FAO statistical database — country agricultural production, trade, prices, food balances. Admin0, annual.

citation: ILO (2024). ILOSTAT — Labour Statistics. International Labour Organization, Geneva.
preprocessing_notes: Use 'agricultural employment as % of total employment' as the rural-labour-availability framing; pair with LSMS-ISA for subnational where present.
limitations: Country-level only; subnational variation requires LSMS-ISA or country uploads.
description: International Labour Organization ILOSTAT — labour-force participation, agricultural employment share, wage indicators. Admin0, annual.

dataset_name: MapSPAM 2020 v2r2 physical crop area, all technologies
citation: IFPRI MapSPAM 2020 v2r2; cloud-optimized distribution: CGIAR Climate Action Data Hub, https://cgiar-climate-data-hub.github.io/catalog/spam2020/
preprocessing_notes: Physical crop area in ha, 46 crop bands in published crop-code order. Select BIND band; coffee includes coff and rcof. Sum component physical areas, divide by geodesic pixel area in ha. Preserve nodata; reject fractions outside [0,1]. Read COG windows, never download full raster. All technologies already includes irrigated and rainfed; do not add them again.
limitations: Modelled allocation, not direct observation. ~5 arc-minute support cannot be sharpened by resampling. Crop fractions retain extent, not suitability strength. Cross-crop overlap must be checked before area totals.
description: Hosted physical-area COG for explicit crop host scoping. Metadata: https://digital-atlas.s3.amazonaws.com/cdh/data/mapspam2020-v2r2/crop-codes.json

dataset_name: Global Pasture Watch dominant grassland class v1
citation: Parente et al. (2024), Global Pasture Watch annual grassland class and extent maps; publisher Earth Engine catalogue.
preprocessing_notes: Select 2020 annual image and dominant_class band. Classes 0 other, 1 cultivated grassland, 2 natural/semi-natural grassland. Derive class fractions before aggregation. Supports pasture context; does not alone confirm grazing.
limitations: Known regional underprediction and cropland confusion. Cultivated class includes managed forage; grazing needs independent confirmation.
description: Publisher-hosted annual 30 m grassland classes.
